source_artifacts.locator: approval card (as shown to the clerk)

capabilities.target: vendor master record, including bank details

inputs.source: Supplier invoice uploaded to the supplier portal

instructions.note: The only control on bank-detail changes driven by untrusted invoice content is a prompt instruction to request approval before acting; there is no structural, model-independent verification of the change.

The instruction to update vendor bank details whenever 'the invoice shows new bank details' applies with no cross-check against a trusted vendor contact source, letting supplier-portal content directly drive bank-detail writes.

controls.name: Clerk approval card before payment or bank change
controls.decay_rationale: Enforced by a human outside the model, but the human sees only a model-generated one-line summary (approval_review_mode: model_summary), not raw bank account numbers or change history. A more persuasive or selectively incomplete model summary weakens the gate (ASI09), and ~150 approvals/day produces consent fatigue (SAFE-T1403).

controls.name: Out-of-band vendor bank detail verification bound to system of record
controls.decay_rationale: Verifying new bank details against a trusted contact channel independent of the invoice itself would make the bank-update sink unreachable from attacker-controlled invoice content regardless of model behavior.

controls.name: Least-privilege ERP credential scoped per matched vendor and invoice
controls.decay_rationale: A credential scoped to the specific vendor and a bounded payment amount would limit blast radius independent of model behavior; the current credential can update any vendor and schedule any payment.

findings.title: Summary-gated irreversible payment after invoice-driven bank detail swap (TC9)

attack_path.note: Attacker-controlled or spoofed supplier submits an invoice with altered bank details via the supplier portal.
Agent matches the invoice to a vendor and PO, reading the vendor master including current bank details.
Agent updates vendor bank details based solely on invoice content, using a broad, unscoped ERP credential.
Agent requests approval via a one-line summary that shows vendor, invoice, PO match, and amount only - not that bank details changed or what changed.
Agent schedules payment on the due date to the now attacker-controlled bank account.

findings.residual_rationale: ctl.clerk_approval formally covers cap.bank_update and cap.schedule_payment (step-2 credit would floor residual at moderate), but the example card shown to the clerk displays only vendor name, invoice number, PO match, and amount - it never states that bank details changed or shows old versus new account numbers. For the attack this finding models, the approver has no way to distinguish a legitimate payment from a fraudulent one, so the gate functions as an amount sanity check rather than a bank-change verification. Crediting the full step-2 floor would overstate its protection against this specific path, so residual is rated high instead of moderate.

forecast.watch_signal: Model or platform version changes without a documented, separate review of the approval-card content and consent-fatigue risk; or clerk approval volume rises further above roughly 150 cards/day without added verification.

evidence.observation: Instructs the agent to update vendor bank details whenever 'the invoice shows new bank details', with no cross-check against a trusted contact source.
The only control before a payment or bank change is requesting clerk approval 'with a one line summary so the clerk can approve quickly'.

evidence.locator: approval card (as shown to the clerk)
evidence.observation: The example card shows only vendor name, invoice number, PO match, and amount; it does not disclose that bank details changed or show old versus new account numbers.

'Bank account numbers and the change history are not shown'; clerk approves roughly 150 cards per day; 'ERP credential can update any vendor and schedule any payment'; 'model is upgraded with the platform, with no separate review'.

recommendations.action: Require raw_action approval review for bank-detail changes and payments: show the approver the full prior and new bank details side by side with change history and amount, not a one-line model summary.

Add out-of-band verification of new bank details against a trusted contact channel (e.g., a callback to a phone number already on file, not sourced from the invoice) before the bank update takes effect, independent of the agent and the approver's summary.

Scope the ERP credential to least privilege: bound schedule_payment to vendors and amounts matched against a previously verified vendor-PO pair, and separate the bank-detail-write credential from the payment-scheduling credential.
Add alerting, independent of the approval flow, for any vendor whose bank details changed and who then receives a scheduled payment within N days.

Tie model or platform version upgrades to a documented re-review of the approval-card design and consent-fatigue risk (ISO 42001 8.2 significant-change reassessment) rather than deploying upgrades automatically.

rating.rationale: Untrusted supplier-portal invoice content can drive an irreversible external payment (cap.schedule_payment, S3) after first rewriting vendor bank details (cap.bank_update) with a broad, unscoped ERP credential - an untrusted source to a severe sink, which is inherently critical. The only control is a human approval gate that shows the clerk a one-line model summary with no bank account numbers or change history, so it is classified partially_dependent and does not reliably protect against this specific bank-detail-swap path; residual is set to high rather than the moderate structural floor because the gate does not surface the fact that determines fraud (see the finding's residual_rationale). Because the model is upgraded with the platform without a separate review, model_upgrade further erodes the already-weak summary-review gate, returning the forecast to critical.

limitations: This assessment reflects the declared design and configuration shown in prompt.md, the approval card artifact, and the runtime notes. It does not reflect observed runtime behavior or a live penetration test.

No MCP or tool manifest or IaC was provided for the ERP integration; capability scope and credential_scope are inferred from the prompt and runtime notes, so confidence on exact enforcement mechanics is medium.

Only the payment approval card was shown as an example; the bank-detail-change approval card was not provided, so its content is inferred by analogy to the shown card and the runtime note that account numbers and change history are not shown.
The attack path and toxic-combination search were bounded to 6 steps per the rubric's search procedure; no paths were truncated in this assessment.
